prerequisites: Knowledge of Graphic Expression at the level of the contents of the first-year subjects Graphic Expression and Computer-Aided Design, and of second-year Mechanical Graphic Engineering or Industrial Graphic Engineering.

The student must handle with ease the precise language for representing a specific idea, object, part or machine, a three-dimensional reality, in a system of exclusively two, such as paper or a computer screen.
Must master the commonly accepted rules and standards used in any industrial drawing, from a mechanical engineer's point of view, both regarding graphic and technological information.

Must master aspects related to the definition of parts and mechanisms in such a way that their configuration and dimensions are perfectly defined and unequivocally interpreted by all persons involved in the subsequent production process.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of industrial design.

syllabus_topics: 11.- RAPID MANUFACTURING OF TOOLS AND FIXTURES
assessment_rules: For the ordinary (June) call, the final grade is calculated as 0.8 multiplied by the in-person exam grade, plus 0.05 multiplied by the sum of Distance Learning Test 1 and 2 grades, plus 0.1 multiplied by the practicals grade. For the extraordinary (September) call, the final grade is 0.9 multiplied by the in-person exam grade, plus 0.1 multiplied by the practicals grade. In both calls, a minimum of 4 points in the in-person exam is required for other components to be summed. Practicals are compulsory and must be passed with a minimum grade of 5; otherwise, the course cannot be passed.
